title: ochq — put your localhost on the internet with one command
description: ochq is a free tunnel: share an app running on your machine with the world at https://name.ochq.uz in one command. For Linux, macOS and Windows. An open-source ngrok alternative.
hero_h1: Put your localhost on the internet with one command
hero_tag: Free, no sign-up. Your app is live at https://name.ochq.uz in seconds.
how_h2: From localhost to the whole world — through one tunnel
how_lead: Your machine is never exposed directly. ochq connects out to the server, builds an encrypted tunnel, and brings incoming requests to you through it.
s1_p: ochq 3000 — the client connects to tunnel.ochq.uz by itself. The connection goes outwards, so there is no port to open on your router.
s2_p: Encrypted with TLS 1.3, and the server's fingerprint is checked. The server hands you an address: https://demo.ochq.uz
s3_p: When someone opens the address, the request reaches the ochq server over HTTPS and travels to your machine on its own stream inside the tunnel.
s4_p: Your app on localhost:3000 answers, and the response returns the same way. Many requests share the one tunnel in parallel.
cap1: the client dials out to the server
cap3: requests arrive from the world through the tunnel
cap4: responses go back through the same tunnel
chip2: Showing a client a site without deploying
chip3: Checking on a phone with real HTTPS
chip5: Runs on your own server too (ochqd)
